messages:
Alex: quick FYI — nightly-5.2 shows a perf regression when kernel selector falls back from nvlink-optimized kernels to generic pcie kernels on 8xA100 mesh nodes. :eyes:

Mira: can you paste the profile? which workload / batch shape?

Alex: repro command:
```
./runtest --topo mesh --fabric nvlink+pcie --model redwood-7b --bsz 8 --seq 2048 --profile trace.json
```
Top-level symptom: steady 12-18% throughput drop, but p99 latency spikes during step boundaries.

Jon: do we see higher all-reduce stall time or is it kv cache thrash?

Alex: profiler snapshot shows both. Timeline snippet:
```
[step 432] compute: 42ms | all-reduce: 18ms | wait: 12ms
kv_miss_rate: 27% -> spike at slice handshake
kernel_switch: nvlink_opt -> generic_pcie at 0.6s
```

Sam: slice handshake?

Alex: when we hand a TP/PP slice across NVLink islands we attempt an nvlink-specialized kernel; fallback to pcie when kernel_lookup fails for that seq_len + sharding combo. That fallback causes extra mem copies and breaks compute/comm overlap for ~2-3 steps.

Mira: any regressions in kernelselect heuristics recently? last week we changed the 'min_seq_for_nvlink' threshold.

Jon: yeah, PR #492 bumped the threshold to avoid bad nvlink kernels on short seqs. Might be too aggressive -> more fallbacks on long seqs with mixed placement.

Infra-bot: scheduled a capture job (trace.json) to s3://perf-captures/nightly/2319998888/trace.json

Alex: experiment: force kernelselector to prefer nvlink even if marginal. Result: restores throughput but p99 jitter earlier in run (likely non-optimal kernel for some micro-batches). Still better than fallback.

Mira: could batching heuristics help? maybe aggregate smaller micro-batches earlier so kernels match more often.

Sam: also the kv cache prefetch window is small, so when kernel changes we get higher kv_miss. Try increasing `kv_prefetch_pages=4` for the mesh test.

Alex: with kv_prefetch_pages=4 + kernelselect override -> throughput +9% and kv_miss -> 8%. p99 spikes reduced.

Jon: good. But for cross-rack EFA nodes we saw different behavior — EFA gives lower all-reduce latency but more variability. Any topology-aware routing changes possible? We could route slices to keep NVLink-local ranks aligned and avoid fallback churn.

Mira: action items:
- Alex: open perf ticket with trace + repro + perf diff (assigned @Alex)
- Jon: run a sweep on kernelselect thresholds and post a matrix (seq_len vs shard_count)
- Sam: test kv_prefetch tuning across fabrics (nvlink vs efa)

Alex: filing ticket now: https://redwood.atlassian.com/browse/RI-1234

Mira: thanks — tagging eng-runtime for visibility. We'll use these results for next kernel selector patch.

Sam: :thumbsup: 

Jon: looping in runtime-ops to consider topology-aware placement later.

Alex: thanks all, I'll attach the trace and the small script to reproduce.
